title: A full lake, a steady catch
hook: A lake of 1,000 fish. You take 130 a year, only 13%. Where does it end?

knows: logistic growth: a population grows fastest at half full (fastest-at-the-bend)
doesNotKnow: that this peak growth sets a hard ceiling on any fixed yearly catch
that a catch just above the ceiling empties a full lake slowly and then fast

misconception: A lake of 1,000 fish can supply 130 a year forever. That is only 13%, and it is full to start with.
objective: The learner can explain that the model lake adds at most 125 fish a year (at half full), so a fixed catch of 130 empties it (in year 55) while a catch of 120 settles near 600.

claims.text: In the lesson's model, a full lake of 1,000 fish with a fixed catch of 130 a year is empty in year 55 (54.9); with 120 a year it settles near 600 (600 at year 60). Other catches on the slider: 80 settles at 800, 90 at 765, 100 at 724, 110 at 673; 140 empties in year 29, 150 in year 21.
claims.source: dN/dt = 0.5N(1 - N/1000) - H, N(0) = 1000, Euler dt 0.001 year, in Demo.tsx simulate(); re-run in node 2026-10-14 (matches the brief's check in company/domains/briefs/life.ecology-body.md).

claims.text: The most the model lake can add in a year is 125 fish, when it is half full (500 fish).
claims.source: Growth 0.5N(1 - N/1000) peaks at N = K/2 with value rK/4 = 0.5 x 1000 / 4 = 125.

claims.text: Any fixed catch above 125 a year takes more than the lake can ever replace, so it empties.
claims.source: 0.5N(1 - N/1000) <= 125 for all N, so dN/dt < 0 everywhere when H > 125.

claims.text: A lake holds at most 1,000 fish and starts full; a few fish multiply fast and a crowded lake barely grows. It is a toy lake: no weather, no luck.
claims.source: Model choice (logistic, r = 0.5, K = 1000, fixed catch; no weather, age structure or chance), stated on the stage and in the reveal. Context for the fact-checker, not on the card: the logistic surplus-production model is the textbook origin of maximum sustainable yield (Schaefer 1954; Hilborn and Walters 1992). Unverified.

recall.question: A pond's fish population can grow by at most 40 fish a year (when half full). It starts full. What happens if you take 45 fish every year?
options: It settles a little below full
It slowly shrinks and then empties
It stays full: 45 is a small share
recall.why: No level of the pond grows by 45 a year, so every year takes more than it adds; it shrinks slowly while crowded, then faster, and empties.
